newsitem.title: JAPAN: Govt shouldn't be formal BOJ board member -- panel.
newsitem.headline: Govt shouldn't be formal BOJ board member -- panel.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's panel studying Bank of Japan (BOJ) reform said on Thursday that government officials should not be formal members of the central bank's policy board.
But if the government and the BOJ considered it necessary, government representatives should be able to attend BOJ policy board meetings, panel head Yasuhiko Torii told a news conference.
Currently, government officials from the Ministry of Finance (MOF) and the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) are members of the policy board, although they do not have the right to vote.
Torii also said panel members wanted the BOJ's executive meetings to be abolished and to make the central bank's policy-making board the sole decision-making body on monetary policy.
"We want the executive meetings as they are now to be abolished and to make one (policy-making) board, both in name and reality," he said.
Although the BOJ's policy board is now responsible for policy matters, financial sources say it is the BOJ's executive meetings that make the decisions the board adopts.
Torii said panel members also agreed that a system by which the government can make suggestions to the board should be devised.
The panel also called for policy-board meetings to be held more frequently. The board now meets twice a week.
The date for the panel's next meeting has yet to be decided, but it will be its last, during which it plans to come up with a final report.
In the next meeting, the panel plans to discuss disclosure of policy-board minutes, a policy aimed at ensuring transparency and accountability.
